summary: Every DELETE handler requires --yes (or an interactive confirm on a TTY stdin and stdout); piped --stdin JSON is non-interactive; POST/PATCH must not retry 5xx or transport errors; MCP path params must be PathEscaped.
reason: Generated mutate handlers skip the advertised confirmation gate — including body-bearing DELETEs such as contents delete-file — and prompting on a TTY stdout while stdin is a pipe consumes the JSON body as the y/N answer. The HTTP client retried every method on 5xx and connection errors (duplicating GitHub writes), and MCP path substitution inserted raw strings so ?, #, and % in content paths were parsed as URL syntax. A regen must preserve fail-closed deletes on all DELETE endpoints (including non-TTY stdin), idempotent-only retries of ambiguous failures, and escaped MCP paths.
validated_outcome: confirmDestructive rejects non-interactive deletes without --yes, including when stdin is piped JSON and stdout is a TTY; POST 500 and POST transport errors issue one HTTP call; GET transport errors still retry; MCP contents path with reserved characters is percent-encoded.
